title: Order line prices, discount and product names are taken from the client
owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry
rationale:
Root cause: BasketItemExtensions.ToOrderItemDTO (src/Ordering.API/Extensions/BasketItemExtensions.cs, ToOrderItemDTO) copies client-supplied UnitPrice/ProductName, and CreateOrderCommandHandler.Handle (CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:43-46) passes them to Order.AddOrderItem with no authoritative lookup. The fix re-prices at the single place where the order aggregate is built (the handler). For every order line it fetches the product's current Name and Price from Catalog.API (GET api/catalog/items/by?ids=..., the same anonymous batch endpoint the WebApp already uses) and passes those to AddOrderItem instead of the client values. Unknown product ids throw OrderingDomainException, so the order is not created. The lookup runs at the top of Handle, before the OrderStarted (basket-clear) event is saved, so a rejected order does not clear the user's basket. Quantity is still client-controlled, as it must be, and is validated by the domain (units > 0). Discount is never client-settable (OrderItemDTO.Discount is init-only and never populated from the request, so it is 0). PictureUrl is cosmetic and left as supplied; it does not affect totals.
New dependency: Ordering.API now makes an HTTP call to catalog-api. Added a typed HttpClient (ICatalogPriceService / CatalogPriceService) using Aspire service discovery ("https+http://catalog-api", the same pattern as WebApp), and .WithReference(catalogApi) on ordering-api in src/eShop.AppHost/AppHost.cs. No new NuGet packages; ServiceDefaults already supplies service discovery and the resilience handler. The call fails closed: if Catalog is unreachable the exception propagates and the order is not created. Reading price from Basket.API instead was rejected because it is gRPC and authenticated per user, and would need the user's token forwarded and a proto reference. Catalog is the price source of truth and its batch endpoint is anonymous. The constructor of CreateOrderCommandHandler gains a parameter, so the one existing test construction was updated.
variants_checked: CreateOrderCommandHandler.Handle: fixed. CreateOrderDraftCommandHandler.Handle (/api/orders/draft): same client-supplied items to AddOrderItem, but it only returns a non-persisted preview DTO and writes nothing, so it was left out of this minimal diff (it could use the same ICatalogPriceService if the preview must also be authoritative). BasketItemExtensions.ToOrderItemDTO/ToOrderItemsDTO: only called by CreateOrderCommand's constructor and the draft handler, so re-pricing in the persisting handler covers it. Order.AddOrderItem is called only from these two handlers (grep of src and tests). The other entry points for CreateOrderCommand (CreateOrderIdentifiedCommandHandler, IdentifiedCommand) dispatch to the same handler. WebApp builds items from the catalog already, so it is unaffected. I did not grep the Basket.API checkout path further since it only publishes the basket-checkout event and does not create orders.
bypass_considered: Attacker sends the lowest-priced real productId with a different ProductName, or sets UnitPrice/OldUnitPrice/Discount to arbitrary values: ignored, because the name and price written to the order always come from Catalog and Discount is not client-settable. Attacker sends a nonexistent ProductId: rejected with OrderingDomainException. Attacker sends the same productId several times: each line is priced identically from Catalog, which is correct and cannot lower the total. Attacker races a price change in Catalog: the order takes the price current at order time, which is the intended semantics. Remaining residual issue (out of scope for this finding): UserId/UserName in CreateOrderRequest are also client-supplied; and Units is still unbounded above, but that is not price tampering.
test_note: Added Handle_prices_order_items_from_catalog_not_from_client to /home/tanis/github/depj-proj/eShop/tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/NewOrderCommandHandlerTest.cs. It sends an item priced 0.01 for a product the mocked catalog prices at 50 and asserts the persisted order line is 50 and the total is 100. Before the change it fails: the old handler stores 0.01, and the handler constructor has no catalog parameter. It was not run (no build access). The existing test in the same file was updated for the new constructor parameter.
review_reason: The handler hunk (`CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:44`) correctly replaces the client `ProductName`/`UnitPrice` with Catalog values, and the endpoint, DTO members and `OrderingDomainException` all exist in source. However, the new `AddHttpClient<ICatalogPriceService, CatalogPriceService>` in `Extensions.cs` omits `.AddApiVersion(...)` although `/api/catalog/items/by` is in a versioned group (`CatalogApi.cs:12-14`) and every existing client pins a version (`WebApp/Extensions/Extensions.cs:34-36`). That would likely cause a 400 and make every order creation throw. The new throw also fires after `AddAndSaveEventAsync` has already persisted the `OrderStartedIntegrationEvent`.
